Find the principal normal vector to that curve at the point $P(2,\frac{1}{2}).$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2t,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ) \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨2,\,t⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,\frac{1}{2})$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2,\frac{1}{2}⟩ \\ ⟨2t,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ \frac{{t}^{2}}{2}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other equation. Therefore, $P(2,\frac{1}{2})$ is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨2,\,t⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}})⟨2,\,t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(⟨2,\,t⟩) \\  & =-\frac{t}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨2,\,t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨0,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}(-t⟨2,t⟩+({t}^{2}+4)⟨0,1⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨-2t,\,4⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{((1)^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨-2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{5}^{3/2}}⟨-2,\,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}‖⟨-1,2⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩}{(\frac{2}{5})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨2,1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2(-1)+1(2)) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-1b8a9865-39bf-545e-aeef-35a531125f5f"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-1b8a9865-39bf-545e-aeef-35a531125f5f" :answer-field/id #uuid "1b8a9865-39bf-545e-aeef-35a531125f5f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-b691e5f8-bc54-56bd-ba8e-fb29b5a7d2f8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-34323a95-3364-5d8b-ae6b-9b380e0bf2c9" "answer-02e39ea1-4cba-57a5-ab90-7a89782cb8d0" "answer-37ad2308-55f9-592a-86af-f156397fae09" "answer-b691e5f8-bc54-56bd-ba8e-fb29b5a7d2f8" "answer-77fd4f80-1bca-57c5-b06d-9f6931a1ae23"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-34323a95-3364-5d8b-ae6b-9b380e0bf2c9" :answer/id #uuid "34323a95-3364-5d8b-ae6b-9b380e0bf2c9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-1,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-02e39ea1-4cba-57a5-ab90-7a89782cb8d0" :answer/id #uuid "02e39ea1-4cba-57a5-ab90-7a89782cb8d0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-1,\sqrt{2}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-37ad2308-55f9-592a-86af-f156397fae09" :answer/id #uuid "37ad2308-55f9-592a-86af-f156397fae09" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\sqrt{2},-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b691e5f8-bc54-56bd-ba8e-fb29b5a7d2f8" :answer/id #uuid "b691e5f8-bc54-56bd-ba8e-fb29b5a7d2f8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-77fd4f80-1bca-57c5-b06d-9f6931a1ae23" :answer/id #uuid "77fd4f80-1bca-57c5-b06d-9f6931a1ae23" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨2,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120252 :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

 
Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=2.$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2})⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}⟨0,\,2,\,2t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}[-2t⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩+({t}^{2}+2)⟨0,\,2,\,2t⟩] \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}⟨4t,\,-2{t}^{2}+4,\,4t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(2) & =\frac{1}{((2)^{2}+2)^{2}}⟨4(2),\,-2(2)^{2}+4,\,4(2)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{36}⟨8,-4,8⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{9}⟨2,-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(2)‖ & =\frac{1}{9}‖⟨2,-1,2⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(2) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(2)}{‖{T}^{′}(2)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{9}⟨2,-1,2⟩}{(\frac{1}{3})}=⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $N$ and $T$ at the point where $t=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}N(2)\cdot T(2) & =⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩\cdot (\frac{1}{6}⟨-2,\,4,\,4⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,4,\,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(-\frac{4}{3}-\frac{4}{3}+\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186117671 :answer-field/correct "answer-524146c4-7e77-5f6d-af6c-ffd660ac28d6" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3d439e47-3587-59b8-90e6-26a8e6ad90ab" "answer-524146c4-7e77-5f6d-af6c-ffd660ac28d6" "answer-fbaf0be8-2245-53a4-8fe1-5686e5bfe610" "answer-b1c1d1e6-bb07-517c-8756-922d8ba89e65"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3d439e47-3587-59b8-90e6-26a8e6ad90ab" :answer/id #uuid "3d439e47-3587-59b8-90e6-26a8e6ad90ab" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨-\frac{2}{3},\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-524146c4-7e77-5f6d-af6c-ffd660ac28d6" :answer/id #uuid "524146c4-7e77-5f6d-af6c-ffd660ac28d6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fbaf0be8-2245-53a4-8fe1-5686e5bfe610" :answer/id #uuid "fbaf0be8-2245-53a4-8fe1-5686e5bfe610" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b1c1d1e6-bb07-517c-8756-922d8ba89e65" :answer/id #uuid "b1c1d1e6-bb07-517c-8756-922d8ba89e65" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120242 :question/worked-solution "First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(0,3,4)$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨0,3,4⟩ \\ 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k & =0\text{ }i+3\text{ }j+4\text{ }k\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components of $i$, $j$, and $k$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{cos}⁡t=0 \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t=3 \\ 4\operatorname{sin}⁡t=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(0,3,4)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(\frac{\pi }{2}).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,k \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+{(-\frac{3}{5})}^{2}+{(-\frac{4}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}+\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,3,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=\frac{-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k}{1}=-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where at $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =(-i)\cdot (-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}(i\cdot j)+\frac{4}{5}(i\cdot k) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/id #uuid "7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/math-academy-id "q-74850" :question/problem "The equations of a curve $r(t)$ and its corresponding unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at an arbitrary point are given below. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at the point $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)).$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)⟩,\,t\ge 0 \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨t,\,1⟩,\,t\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1))$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)⟩ \\ ⟨\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)⟩ & =⟨\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}=\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other equation. Therefore, $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1))$ is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨t,\,1⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}})⟨t,\,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =-\frac{t}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨t,\,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨1,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}[-⟨{t}^{2},\,t⟩+({t}^{2}+1)\cdot ⟨1,\,0⟩] \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,\,-t⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{({1}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}‖⟨1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,1⟩\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-1) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-9023e46d-1d99-5286-baf3-0582b7f8b0a3"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-9023e46d-1d99-5286-baf3-0582b7f8b0a3" :answer-field/id #uuid "9023e46d-1d99-5286-baf3-0582b7f8b0a3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-63b699bf-e6d8-5ef0-9f70-0ede7e9e9edb" :answer-field/choices ["answer-b10046fc-c183-59e3-ae38-7e794395db17" "answer-63b699bf-e6d8-5ef0-9f70-0ede7e9e9edb" "answer-a7b0f6c4-1c16-5380-8c5e-e758a32ebbc5" "answer-4b50b45b-e31f-500e-9496-cc48c7886b21" "answer-f08e5f05-4e3e-5da4-b635-cb93796cbc71"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b10046fc-c183-59e3-ae38-7e794395db17" :answer/id #uuid "b10046fc-c183-59e3-ae38-7e794395db17" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,\,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-63b699bf-e6d8-5ef0-9f70-0ede7e9e9edb" :answer/id #uuid "63b699bf-e6d8-5ef0-9f70-0ede7e9e9edb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,\,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a7b0f6c4-1c16-5380-8c5e-e758a32ebbc5" :answer/id #uuid "a7b0f6c4-1c16-5380-8c5e-e758a32ebbc5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨-2,\,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4b50b45b-e31f-500e-9496-cc48c7886b21" :answer/id #uuid "4b50b45b-e31f-500e-9496-cc48c7886b21" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨-1,\,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f08e5f05-4e3e-5da4-b635-cb93796cbc71" :answer/id #uuid "f08e5f05-4e3e-5da4-b635-cb93796cbc71" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,\,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-f357a402-4ed9-5871-9002-ee2ada823334" :question/id #uuid "f357a402-4ed9-5871-9002-ee2ada823334" :question/math-academy-id "q-358780" :question/problem "$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{13}(-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+12\,k).
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given above. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$i\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{13}(-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+12\,k)) \\  & =\frac{1}{13}(-5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i-5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12)\,k) \\  & =\frac{5}{13}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{5}{13}‖\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j‖ \\  & =\frac{5}{13}\sqrt{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5}{13}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{5}{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{5}{13}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)}{\frac{5}{13}} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}

$\,,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡2t+{sin}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\  & =-2⟨0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =|-2|\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{-2⟨0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩}{2} \\  & =⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-11c25002-d570-5188-8443-f9f108b5d95d"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-11c25002-d570-5188-8443-f9f108b5d95d" :answer-field/id #uuid "11c25002-d570-5188-8443-f9f108b5d95d" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-ba0cef59-7cae-59d5-aee5-dae91a214aef" :answer-field/choices ["answer-ba0cef59-7cae-59d5-aee5-dae91a214aef"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ba0cef59-7cae-59d5-aee5-dae91a214aef" :answer/id #uuid "ba0cef59-7cae-59d5-aee5-dae91a214aef" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-\sin(2t)" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-bc713dbc-3c1f-5a9c-8a2b-b4377300bc92" :question/id #uuid "bc713dbc-3c1f-5a9c-8a2b-b4377300bc92" :question/math-academy-id "q-75410" :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨0,3⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{t}{({t}^{2}+9)\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{0}{({0}^{2}+9)\sqrt{{0}^{2}+9}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+9}}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{3}⟨1,0⟩}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{3}q(0)\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨0,3⟩\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(0\cdot 1+3\cdot 0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(0+0) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-6e89c597-7b48-520a-9aa5-d249aa23a780"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-6e89c597-7b48-520a-9aa5-d249aa23a780" :answer-field/id #uuid "6e89c597-7b48-520a-9aa5-d249aa23a780" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-9b75c8af-bc89-5538-be8b-284dd95d1b81" :answer-field/choices ["answer-512116d3-97dd-54be-bc16-10567d150eb8" "answer-54e8dd13-f4d3-59cf-aea8-647ea53c3240" "answer-09429f0b-5a31-576e-b53c-7a9c9089a259" "answer-4df4322e-2ca8-59b0-b25f-d74e9d345855" "answer-9b75c8af-bc89-5538-be8b-284dd95d1b81"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-512116d3-97dd-54be-bc16-10567d150eb8" :answer/id #uuid "512116d3-97dd-54be-bc16-10567d150eb8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}⟨1,3⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-54e8dd13-f4d3-59cf-aea8-647ea53c3240" :answer/id #uuid "54e8dd13-f4d3-59cf-aea8-647ea53c3240" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-09429f0b-5a31-576e-b53c-7a9c9089a259" :answer/id #uuid "09429f0b-5a31-576e-b53c-7a9c9089a259" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4df4322e-2ca8-59b0-b25f-d74e9d345855" :answer/id #uuid "4df4322e-2ca8-59b0-b25f-d74e9d345855" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9b75c8af-bc89-5538-be8b-284dd95d1b81" :answer/id #uuid "9b75c8af-bc89-5538-be8b-284dd95d1b81" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨1,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-86bd8ee0-d1c5-5e4f-9534-8a4e93bb860c" :question/id #uuid "86bd8ee0-d1c5-5e4f-9534-8a4e93bb860c" :question/math-academy-id "q-127597" :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1)=⟨1,\sqrt{6},3⟩,\,{q}^{′}(1)=⟨0,\sqrt{6},6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{6t}{{(1+3{t}^{2})}^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =-\frac{6(1)}{{(1+3(1)^{2})}^{2}}\cdot q(1)+\frac{1}{1+3(1)^{2}}\cdot {q}^{′}(1) \\  & =-\frac{3}{8}⟨1,\sqrt{6},3⟩+\frac{1}{4}⟨0,\sqrt{6},6⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(-3⟨1,\sqrt{6},3⟩+2⟨0,\sqrt{6},6⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-\sqrt{6})^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{24} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{8}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{6}}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{4}q(1)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{6}}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨1,\sqrt{6},3⟩\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{6}}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{8\sqrt{6}}(1\cdot (-3)+\sqrt{6}\cdot (-\sqrt{6})+3\cdot 3) \\  & =\frac{1}{8\sqrt{6}}(-3-6+9) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-2dcaf563-74bd-51e5-bbaf-671c2387e005"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨0,1,1⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨0,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{2t}}{({e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{{e}^{0}}{({e}^{0}+1)^{3/2}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{0}+1}}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}⟨0,1,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}(-⟨0,1,1⟩+2⟨0,1,0⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}q(0)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0(0)+1(1)+1(-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-1) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-be28023f-b4e1-527a-9fd6-a55af9912450"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-be28023f-b4e1-527a-9fd6-a55af9912450" :answer-field/id #uuid "be28023f-b4e1-527a-9fd6-a55af9912450" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-e0ec4419-91f6-5d58-9711-3de15ef93020" :answer-field/choices ["answer-f911a805-3f13-582e-9b9e-8ec61aec91fe" "answer-625e5e39-ae98-52ef-bfcc-de3e0bace052" "answer-18b10125-03d9-569f-b489-2af1cd51651f" "answer-f33db979-e5fc-564b-9e72-04e2ed505855" "answer-e0ec4419-91f6-5d58-9711-3de15ef93020"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f911a805-3f13-582e-9b9e-8ec61aec91fe" :answer/id #uuid "f911a805-3f13-582e-9b9e-8ec61aec91fe" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}⟨0,1,\sqrt{2}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-625e5e39-ae98-52ef-bfcc-de3e0bace052" :answer/id #uuid "625e5e39-ae98-52ef-bfcc-de3e0bace052" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{2},1,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-18b10125-03d9-569f-b489-2af1cd51651f" :answer/id #uuid "18b10125-03d9-569f-b489-2af1cd51651f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}⟨2,1,-2⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f33db979-e5fc-564b-9e72-04e2ed505855" :answer/id #uuid "f33db979-e5fc-564b-9e72-04e2ed505855" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-1,0,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e0ec4419-91f6-5d58-9711-3de15ef93020" :answer/id #uuid "e0ec4419-91f6-5d58-9711-3de15ef93020" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120520 :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by 

$$
T(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(\frac{\pi }{2})=i,\,{q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})=-j.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot q(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot q(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot q(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot {q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & ={q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =-j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖} \\  & =\frac{-j}{1} \\  & =-j\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $N$ and $T$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})q(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot (-j) \\  & =(i)\cdot (-j) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119234 :answer-field/correct 17592186119235 :answer-field/choices ["answer-999190e0-5bbc-5bc3-8758-e312658c0541" "answer-283cc10c-c7dc-5d42-98bb-ff049bacb22b" "answer-bfdd62a5-1439-52d3-bd50-2dddd660304c" "answer-28cf7792-7abc-5ff9-b607-d63d93877d58"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-999190e0-5bbc-5bc3-8758-e312658c0541" :answer/id #uuid "999190e0-5bbc-5bc3-8758-e312658c0541" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-283cc10c-c7dc-5d42-98bb-ff049bacb22b" :answer/id #uuid "283cc10c-c7dc-5d42-98bb-ff049bacb22b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bfdd62a5-1439-52d3-bd50-2dddd660304c" :answer/id #uuid "bfdd62a5-1439-52d3-bd50-2dddd660304c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\,i-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-28cf7792-7abc-5ff9-b607-d63d93877d58" :answer/id #uuid "28cf7792-7abc-5ff9-b607-d63d93877d58" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "i+j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121148 :tutorial/content "The **principal normal vector** to a curve $C$ at a point $P$ is a unit vector that 

- is perpendicular to the unit tangent vector, and

- points in the direction that the curve is bending.

In general, if the unit tangent vector is given by $\mathbf T(t),$ then the principal normal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf N(t)= \dfrac{\mathbf T'(t)}{\|\mathbf T'(t)\|},
$$

where it is assumed that $\|\mathbf T'(t)\|\neq 0.$

To demonstrate, suppose that the curve $C$ is parametrized by the vector function 

$$
\mathbf f(t) = \left\langle 2\cos t, \: 2\sin t \right\rangle, \qquad t \in [0, \pi].
$$

We will compute the principal normal vector at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}.$

First, using the formula for the unit tangent, $\mathbf T(t) = \dfrac{\mathbf f'(t)}{||\mathbf f'(t)||},$ we find that the general unit tangent vector is

$$
\mathbf T(t)= \left\langle {-\sin t}, \cos t\right\rangle.
$$

Now, when $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ we have the point $P(\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}).$ The unit tangent vector $\mathbf{T}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ and the principal normal vector $\mathbf{N}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ at this point are shown below:

![](images/d0/d0a30a44bb825a8a12ca54153b6223b9bf0c2b754245b21650a5664db5e1647e.png)

To calculate the principal normal vector, we start by calculating the derivative of the unit tangent function. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general principal normal vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{||{T}^{′}(t)||} \\  & =\frac{⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{\sqrt{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t}} \\  & =\frac{⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{\sqrt{1}} \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find $\mathbf N\left(\dfrac\pi 4\right),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, it's easy to check that $\mathbf T'(t)$ and $\mathbf N'(t)$ are perpendicular for all $t$ by computing the dot product and showing that we get zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t)\cdot N(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\cdot ⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121149 :tutorial/content "Let $\mathbf T(t)$ be the unit tangent vector to some differentiable vector-valued function. Since $||\mathbf T(t)|| = 1,$ and $\mathbf T(t)$ is obviously parallel to itself, we must have

$$
\mathbf T(t) \cdot \mathbf T(t) = 1.
$$

Differentiating the above relationship with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\mathbf T'(t) \cdot \mathbf T(t) + \mathbf T(t) \cdot \mathbf T'(t) = 0,
$$

which can be simplified as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t)\cdot T(t)+{T}^{′}(t)\cdot T(t) & =0 \\ 2{T}^{′}(t)\cdot T(t) & =0 \\ {T}^{′}(t)\cdot T(t) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, provided that $\mathbf T'(t)\neq \mathbf 0,$ then it must be the case that $\mathbf T'(t)$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf T(t).$

The vector $\mathbf T'(t)$ measures the rate of change of $\mathbf T(t).$ However, since $\mathbf T(t)$ is a unit vector for all $t,$ it changes only in its direction. The vector $\mathbf T'(t)$ measures this rate of change in direction. 

To form the principal normal $\mathbf N(t),$ we normalize $\mathbf T'(t),$ which leads to the definition

$$
\mathbf N(t) = \dfrac{\mathbf T'(t)}{||\mathbf T'(t)||}.
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121150 :tutorial/content "Consider the straight line given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t\,[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

 

If we attempt to calculate its principal normal vector, we will get an interesting result. First, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and $\|\mathbf r'(t)\|
\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[\begin{aligned}-2+5t \\ 1 \\ \sqrt{2}t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}] \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=\sqrt{27}=3\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\,[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in the case of a straight line, $\mathbf T(t)$ is simply the (normalized) direction vector, as we would expect. 

Next, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\,[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2})\end{aligned}]=0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\mathbf{T}'(t)$ is the zero vector, we can't normalize it as usual. If we try to apply the usual formula we get an undefined result due to division by zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{0}{‖0‖}=\frac{0}{0}=\text{undefined}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a straight line does not have a principal normal.

The intuition behind this result is that the principal normal points in the direction in which a curve is bending, but a straight line does not bend at all." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120013 :activity/expected-seconds 1020.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120641 :step/math-academy-id 626149 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120642 :step/math-academy-id 626150 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120643 :step/math-academy-id 626153 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120644 :step/math-academy-id 626156 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120645 :step/math-academy-id 626157 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120646 :step/math-academy-id 626160 :db/ensure [:step/validate]}]

{"source" ":org/Math-Academy" "forms" [[:db/retract 17592186117671 :answer-field/choices 17592186117672] [:db/retract 17592186117671 :answer-field/choices 17592186117673] [:db/retract 17592186117671 :answer-field/choices 17592186117675] [:db/retract 17592186117671 :answer-field/choices 17592186117676] [:db/retract 17592186120242 :question/answer-fields 17592186117611] [:db/retract 17592186119234 :answer-field/choices 17592186119236] [:db/retract 17592186119234 :answer-field/choices 17592186119237] [:db/retract 17592186119234 :answer-field/choices 17592186119238] [:db/retract 17592186119234 :answer-field/choices 17592186119239] {:db/id 17592186119785 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a" "question-7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119786 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-f357a402-4ed9-5871-9002-ee2ada823334" "question-7043d5b3-b126-54ab-a0bc-9816029b7532"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119787 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-bc713dbc-3c1f-5a9c-8a2b-b4377300bc92" "question-86bd8ee0-d1c5-5e4f-9534-8a4e93bb860c" "question-35b2b5dc-be5b-531e-92b7-e1931e890d8a"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a" :question/id #uuid "f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a" :question/math-academy-id "q-127379" :question/problem "The equations of a curve $r(t)$ and its corresponding unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at an arbitrary point are given below. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at the point $P(2,\frac{1}{2}).$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2t,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ) \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨2,\,t⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,\frac{1}{2})$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2,\frac{1}{2}⟩ \\ ⟨2t,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ \frac{{t}^{2}}{2}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other equation. Therefore, $P(2,\frac{1}{2})$ is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨2,\,t⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}})⟨2,\,t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(⟨2,\,t⟩) \\  & =-\frac{t}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨2,\,t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨0,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}(-t⟨2,t⟩+({t}^{2}+4)⟨0,1⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨-2t,\,4⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{((1)^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨-2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{5}^{3/2}}⟨-2,\,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}‖⟨-1,2⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩}{(\frac{2}{5})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨2,1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2(-1)+1(2)) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-1b8a9865-39bf-545e-aeef-35a531125f5f"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-1b8a9865-39bf-545e-aeef-35a531125f5f" :answer-field/id #uuid "1b8a9865-39bf-545e-aeef-35a531125f5f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-b691e5f8-bc54-56bd-ba8e-fb29b5a7d2f8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-34323a95-3364-5d8b-ae6b-9b380e0bf2c9" "answer-02e39ea1-4cba-57a5-ab90-7a89782cb8d0" "answer-37ad2308-55f9-592a-86af-f156397fae09" "answer-b691e5f8-bc54-56bd-ba8e-fb29b5a7d2f8" "answer-77fd4f80-1bca-57c5-b06d-9f6931a1ae23"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-34323a95-3364-5d8b-ae6b-9b380e0bf2c9" :answer/id #uuid "34323a95-3364-5d8b-ae6b-9b380e0bf2c9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-1,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-02e39ea1-4cba-57a5-ab90-7a89782cb8d0" :answer/id #uuid "02e39ea1-4cba-57a5-ab90-7a89782cb8d0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-1,\sqrt{2}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-37ad2308-55f9-592a-86af-f156397fae09" :answer/id #uuid "37ad2308-55f9-592a-86af-f156397fae09" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\sqrt{2},-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b691e5f8-bc54-56bd-ba8e-fb29b5a7d2f8" :answer/id #uuid "b691e5f8-bc54-56bd-ba8e-fb29b5a7d2f8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-77fd4f80-1bca-57c5-b06d-9f6931a1ae23" :answer/id #uuid "77fd4f80-1bca-57c5-b06d-9f6931a1ae23" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨2,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120252 :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

 
Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=2.$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2})⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}⟨0,\,2,\,2t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}[-2t⟨-2,\,2t,\,{t}^{2}⟩+({t}^{2}+2)⟨0,\,2,\,2t⟩] \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}⟨4t,\,-2{t}^{2}+4,\,4t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(2) & =\frac{1}{((2)^{2}+2)^{2}}⟨4(2),\,-2(2)^{2}+4,\,4(2)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{36}⟨8,-4,8⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{9}⟨2,-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(2)‖ & =\frac{1}{9}‖⟨2,-1,2⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(2) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(2)}{‖{T}^{′}(2)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{9}⟨2,-1,2⟩}{(\frac{1}{3})}=⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $N$ and $T$ at the point where $t=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}N(2)\cdot T(2) & =⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩\cdot (\frac{1}{6}⟨-2,\,4,\,4⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,4,\,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(-\frac{4}{3}-\frac{4}{3}+\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186117671 :answer-field/correct "answer-524146c4-7e77-5f6d-af6c-ffd660ac28d6" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3d439e47-3587-59b8-90e6-26a8e6ad90ab" "answer-524146c4-7e77-5f6d-af6c-ffd660ac28d6" "answer-fbaf0be8-2245-53a4-8fe1-5686e5bfe610" "answer-b1c1d1e6-bb07-517c-8756-922d8ba89e65"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3d439e47-3587-59b8-90e6-26a8e6ad90ab" :answer/id #uuid "3d439e47-3587-59b8-90e6-26a8e6ad90ab" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨-\frac{2}{3},\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-524146c4-7e77-5f6d-af6c-ffd660ac28d6" :answer/id #uuid "524146c4-7e77-5f6d-af6c-ffd660ac28d6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fbaf0be8-2245-53a4-8fe1-5686e5bfe610" :answer/id #uuid "fbaf0be8-2245-53a4-8fe1-5686e5bfe610" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨\frac{2}{3},-\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b1c1d1e6-bb07-517c-8756-922d8ba89e65" :answer/id #uuid "b1c1d1e6-bb07-517c-8756-922d8ba89e65" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120242 :question/worked-solution "First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(0,3,4)$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨0,3,4⟩ \\ 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k & =0\text{ }i+3\text{ }j+4\text{ }k\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components of $i$, $j$, and $k$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{cos}⁡t=0 \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t=3 \\ 4\operatorname{sin}⁡t=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(0,3,4)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(\frac{\pi }{2}).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,k \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+{(-\frac{3}{5})}^{2}+{(-\frac{4}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}+\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,3,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=\frac{-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k}{1}=-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where at $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =(-i)\cdot (-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}(i\cdot j)+\frac{4}{5}(i\cdot k) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/id #uuid "7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/math-academy-id "q-74850" :question/problem "The equations of a curve $r(t)$ and its corresponding unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at an arbitrary point are given below. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at the point $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)).$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)⟩,\,t\ge 0 \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨t,\,1⟩,\,t\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1))$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)⟩ \\ ⟨\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)⟩ & =⟨\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}=\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other equation. Therefore, $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1))$ is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨t,\,1⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}})⟨t,\,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =-\frac{t}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨t,\,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨1,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}[-⟨{t}^{2},\,t⟩+({t}^{2}+1)\cdot ⟨1,\,0⟩] \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,\,-t⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{({1}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}‖⟨1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,1⟩\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-1) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-9023e46d-1d99-5286-baf3-0582b7f8b0a3"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-9023e46d-1d99-5286-baf3-0582b7f8b0a3" :answer-field/id #uuid "9023e46d-1d99-5286-baf3-0582b7f8b0a3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-63b699bf-e6d8-5ef0-9f70-0ede7e9e9edb" :answer-field/choices ["answer-b10046fc-c183-59e3-ae38-7e794395db17" "answer-63b699bf-e6d8-5ef0-9f70-0ede7e9e9edb" "answer-a7b0f6c4-1c16-5380-8c5e-e758a32ebbc5" "answer-4b50b45b-e31f-500e-9496-cc48c7886b21" "answer-f08e5f05-4e3e-5da4-b635-cb93796cbc71"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b10046fc-c183-59e3-ae38-7e794395db17" :answer/id #uuid "b10046fc-c183-59e3-ae38-7e794395db17" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,\,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-63b699bf-e6d8-5ef0-9f70-0ede7e9e9edb" :answer/id #uuid "63b699bf-e6d8-5ef0-9f70-0ede7e9e9edb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,\,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a7b0f6c4-1c16-5380-8c5e-e758a32ebbc5" :answer/id #uuid "a7b0f6c4-1c16-5380-8c5e-e758a32ebbc5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨-2,\,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4b50b45b-e31f-500e-9496-cc48c7886b21" :answer/id #uuid "4b50b45b-e31f-500e-9496-cc48c7886b21" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨-1,\,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f08e5f05-4e3e-5da4-b635-cb93796cbc71" :answer/id #uuid "f08e5f05-4e3e-5da4-b635-cb93796cbc71" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,\,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-f357a402-4ed9-5871-9002-ee2ada823334" :question/id #uuid "f357a402-4ed9-5871-9002-ee2ada823334" :question/math-academy-id "q-358780" :question/problem "$$

$i\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$

"question-7043d5b3-b126-54ab-a0bc-9816029b7532" :question/id #uuid "7043d5b3-b126-54ab-a0bc-9816029b7532" :question/math-academy-id "q-223120" :question/problem "Given the curve $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{3},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$⟨\,0\,,$
{{field-1}}
$\,,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡2t+{sin}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\  & =-2⟨0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =|-2|\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{-2⟨0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩}{2} \\  & =⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-11c25002-d570-5188-8443-f9f108b5d95d"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-11c25002-d570-5188-8443-f9f108b5d95d" :answer-field/id #uuid "11c25002-d570-5188-8443-f9f108b5d95d" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-ba0cef59-7cae-59d5-aee5-dae91a214aef" :answer-field/choices ["answer-ba0cef59-7cae-59d5-aee5-dae91a214aef"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ba0cef59-7cae-59d5-aee5-dae91a214aef" :answer/id #uuid "ba0cef59-7cae-59d5-aee5-dae91a214aef" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-\sin(2t)" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-bc713dbc-3c1f-5a9c-8a2b-b4377300bc92" :question/id #uuid "bc713dbc-3c1f-5a9c-8a2b-b4377300bc92" :question/math-academy-id "q-75410" :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨0,3⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{t}{({t}^{2}+9)\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+9}}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{0}{({0}^{2}+9)\sqrt{{0}^{2}+9}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+9}}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{3}⟨1,0⟩}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{3}q(0)\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨0,3⟩\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(0\cdot 1+3\cdot 0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(0+0) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-6e89c597-7b48-520a-9aa5-d249aa23a780"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-6e89c597-7b48-520a-9aa5-d249aa23a780" :answer-field/id #uuid "6e89c597-7b48-520a-9aa5-d249aa23a780" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-9b75c8af-bc89-5538-be8b-284dd95d1b81" :answer-field/choices ["answer-512116d3-97dd-54be-bc16-10567d150eb8" "answer-54e8dd13-f4d3-59cf-aea8-647ea53c3240" "answer-09429f0b-5a31-576e-b53c-7a9c9089a259" "answer-4df4322e-2ca8-59b0-b25f-d74e9d345855" "answer-9b75c8af-bc89-5538-be8b-284dd95d1b81"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-512116d3-97dd-54be-bc16-10567d150eb8" :answer/id #uuid "512116d3-97dd-54be-bc16-10567d150eb8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}⟨1,3⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-54e8dd13-f4d3-59cf-aea8-647ea53c3240" :answer/id #uuid "54e8dd13-f4d3-59cf-aea8-647ea53c3240" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-09429f0b-5a31-576e-b53c-7a9c9089a259" :answer/id #uuid "09429f0b-5a31-576e-b53c-7a9c9089a259" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4df4322e-2ca8-59b0-b25f-d74e9d345855" :answer/id #uuid "4df4322e-2ca8-59b0-b25f-d74e9d345855" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9b75c8af-bc89-5538-be8b-284dd95d1b81" :answer/id #uuid "9b75c8af-bc89-5538-be8b-284dd95d1b81" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨1,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-86bd8ee0-d1c5-5e4f-9534-8a4e93bb860c" :question/id #uuid "86bd8ee0-d1c5-5e4f-9534-8a4e93bb860c" :question/math-academy-id "q-127597" :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1)=⟨1,\sqrt{6},3⟩,\,{q}^{′}(1)=⟨0,\sqrt{6},6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{6t}{{(1+3{t}^{2})}^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{1+3{t}^{2}}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =-\frac{6(1)}{{(1+3(1)^{2})}^{2}}\cdot q(1)+\frac{1}{1+3(1)^{2}}\cdot {q}^{′}(1) \\  & =-\frac{3}{8}⟨1,\sqrt{6},3⟩+\frac{1}{4}⟨0,\sqrt{6},6⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(-3⟨1,\sqrt{6},3⟩+2⟨0,\sqrt{6},6⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-\sqrt{6})^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{24} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{8}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{6}}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩\end{aligned}

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{4}q(1)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{6}}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨1,\sqrt{6},3⟩\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{6}}⟨-3,-\sqrt{6},3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{8\sqrt{6}}(1\cdot (-3)+\sqrt{6}\cdot (-\sqrt{6})+3\cdot 3) \\  & =\frac{1}{8\sqrt{6}}(-3-6+9) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}

"question-35b2b5dc-be5b-531e-92b7-e1931e890d8a" :question/id #uuid "35b2b5dc-be5b-531e-92b7-e1931e890d8a" :question/math-academy-id "q-127596" :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨0,1,1⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨0,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{2t}}{({e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{{e}^{0}}{({e}^{0}+1)^{3/2}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{0}+1}}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}⟨0,1,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}(-⟨0,1,1⟩+2⟨0,1,0⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}q(0)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0(0)+1(1)+1(-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-1) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-be28023f-b4e1-527a-9fd6-a55af9912450"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-be28023f-b4e1-527a-9fd6-a55af9912450" :answer-field/id #uuid "be28023f-b4e1-527a-9fd6-a55af9912450" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-e0ec4419-91f6-5d58-9711-3de15ef93020" :answer-field/choices ["answer-f911a805-3f13-582e-9b9e-8ec61aec91fe" "answer-625e5e39-ae98-52ef-bfcc-de3e0bace052" "answer-18b10125-03d9-569f-b489-2af1cd51651f" "answer-f33db979-e5fc-564b-9e72-04e2ed505855" "answer-e0ec4419-91f6-5d58-9711-3de15ef93020"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f911a805-3f13-582e-9b9e-8ec61aec91fe" :answer/id #uuid "f911a805-3f13-582e-9b9e-8ec61aec91fe" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}⟨0,1,\sqrt{2}⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-625e5e39-ae98-52ef-bfcc-de3e0bace052" :answer/id #uuid "625e5e39-ae98-52ef-bfcc-de3e0bace052" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{2},1,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-18b10125-03d9-569f-b489-2af1cd51651f" :answer/id #uuid "18b10125-03d9-569f-b489-2af1cd51651f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}⟨2,1,-2⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f33db979-e5fc-564b-9e72-04e2ed505855" :answer/id #uuid "f33db979-e5fc-564b-9e72-04e2ed505855" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-1,0,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e0ec4419-91f6-5d58-9711-3de15ef93020" :answer/id #uuid "e0ec4419-91f6-5d58-9711-3de15ef93020" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,1,-1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120520 :question/problem "The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by 

$$
T(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(\frac{\pi }{2})=i,\,{q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})=-j.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot q(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot q(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot q(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot {q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & ={q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =-j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖} \\  & =\frac{-j}{1} \\  & =-j\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $N$ and $T$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})q(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot (-j) \\  & =(i)\cdot (-j) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119234 :answer-field/correct 17592186119235 :answer-field/choices ["answer-999190e0-5bbc-5bc3-8758-e312658c0541" "answer-283cc10c-c7dc-5d42-98bb-ff049bacb22b" "answer-bfdd62a5-1439-52d3-bd50-2dddd660304c" "answer-28cf7792-7abc-5ff9-b607-d63d93877d58"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-999190e0-5bbc-5bc3-8758-e312658c0541" :answer/id #uuid "999190e0-5bbc-5bc3-8758-e312658c0541" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-283cc10c-c7dc-5d42-98bb-ff049bacb22b" :answer/id #uuid "283cc10c-c7dc-5d42-98bb-ff049bacb22b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bfdd62a5-1439-52d3-bd50-2dddd660304c" :answer/id #uuid "bfdd62a5-1439-52d3-bd50-2dddd660304c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\,i-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-28cf7792-7abc-5ff9-b607-d63d93877d58" :answer/id #uuid "28cf7792-7abc-5ff9-b607-d63d93877d58" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "i+j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121148 :tutorial/content "The **principal normal vector** to a curve $C$ at a point $P$ is a unit vector that 

- is perpendicular to the unit tangent vector, and

- points in the direction that the curve is bending.

In general, if the unit tangent vector is given by $\mathbf T(t),$ then the principal normal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf N(t)= \dfrac{\mathbf T'(t)}{\|\mathbf T'(t)\|},
$$

where it is assumed that $\|\mathbf T'(t)\|\neq 0.$

To demonstrate, suppose that the curve $C$ is parametrized by the vector function 

$$
\mathbf f(t) = \left\langle 2\cos t, \: 2\sin t \right\rangle, \qquad t \in [0, \pi].
$$

We will compute the principal normal vector at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}.$

First, using the formula for the unit tangent, $\mathbf T(t) = \dfrac{\mathbf f'(t)}{||\mathbf f'(t)||},$ we find that the general unit tangent vector is

$$
\mathbf T(t)= \left\langle {-\sin t}, \cos t\right\rangle.
$$

Now, when $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ we have the point $P(\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}).$ The unit tangent vector $\mathbf{T}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ and the principal normal vector $\mathbf{N}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ at this point are shown below:

![](images/d0/d0a30a44bb825a8a12ca54153b6223b9bf0c2b754245b21650a5664db5e1647e.png)

To calculate the principal normal vector, we start by calculating the derivative of the unit tangent function. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general principal normal vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{||{T}^{′}(t)||} \\  & =\frac{⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{\sqrt{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t}} \\  & =\frac{⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{\sqrt{1}} \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find $\mathbf N\left(\dfrac\pi 4\right),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, it's easy to check that $\mathbf T'(t)$ and $\mathbf N'(t)$ are perpendicular for all $t$ by computing the dot product and showing that we get zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t)\cdot N(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\cdot ⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121149 :tutorial/content "Let $\mathbf T(t)$ be the unit tangent vector to some differentiable vector-valued function. Since $||\mathbf T(t)|| = 1,$ and $\mathbf T(t)$ is obviously parallel to itself, we must have

$$
\mathbf T(t) \cdot \mathbf T(t) = 1.
$$

Differentiating the above relationship with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\mathbf T'(t) \cdot \mathbf T(t) + \mathbf T(t) \cdot \mathbf T'(t) = 0,
$$

which can be simplified as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t)\cdot T(t)+{T}^{′}(t)\cdot T(t) & =0 \\ 2{T}^{′}(t)\cdot T(t) & =0 \\ {T}^{′}(t)\cdot T(t) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, provided that $\mathbf T'(t)\neq \mathbf 0,$ then it must be the case that $\mathbf T'(t)$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf T(t).$

The vector $\mathbf T'(t)$ measures the rate of change of $\mathbf T(t).$ However, since $\mathbf T(t)$ is a unit vector for all $t,$ it changes only in its direction. The vector $\mathbf T'(t)$ measures this rate of change in direction. 

To form the principal normal $\mathbf N(t),$ we normalize $\mathbf T'(t),$ which leads to the definition

$$
\mathbf N(t) = \dfrac{\mathbf T'(t)}{||\mathbf T'(t)||}.
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121150 :tutorial/content "Consider the straight line given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t\,[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

 

If we attempt to calculate its principal normal vector, we will get an interesting result. First, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and $\|\mathbf r'(t)\|
\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[\begin{aligned}-2+5t \\ 1 \\ \sqrt{2}t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}] \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=\sqrt{27}=3\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\,[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in the case of a straight line, $\mathbf T(t)$ is simply the (normalized) direction vector, as we would expect. 

Next, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\,[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2})\end{aligned}]=0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\mathbf{T}'(t)$ is the zero vector, we can't normalize it as usual. If we try to apply the usual formula we get an undefined result due to division by zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{0}{‖0‖}=\frac{0}{0}=\text{undefined}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a straight line does not have a principal normal.

The intuition behind this result is that the principal normal points in the direction in which a curve is bending, but a straight line does not bend at all." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120013 :activity/expected-seconds 1020.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120641 :step/math-academy-id 626149 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120642 :step/math-academy-id 626150 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120643 :step/math-academy-id 626153 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120644 :step/math-academy-id 626156 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120645 :step/math-academy-id 626157 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120646 :step/math-academy-id 626160 :db/ensure [:step/validate]}] "assertions" [["question-f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a" :question/id #uuid "f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a"] ["question-f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a" :question/math-academy-id "q-127379"] ["question-f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a" :question/problem "The equations of a curve $r(t)$ and its corresponding unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at an arbitrary point are given below. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at the point $P(2,\frac{1}{2}).$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2t,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ) \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨2,\,t⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,\frac{1}{2})$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2,\frac{1}{2}⟩ \\ ⟨2t,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ \frac{{t}^{2}}{2}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other equation. Therefore, $P(2,\frac{1}{2})$ is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨2,\,t⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}})⟨2,\,t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(⟨2,\,t⟩) \\  & =-\frac{t}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨2,\,t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨0,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}(-t⟨2,t⟩+({t}^{2}+4)⟨0,1⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{{({t}^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨-2t,\,4⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{((1)^{2}+4)}^{3/2}}⟨-2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{5}^{3/2}}⟨-2,\,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}‖⟨-1,2⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩}{(\frac{2}{5})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨2,1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2(-1)+1(2)) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-f08885d9-557e-5e55-b967-a7cb452a9e2a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-1b8a9865-39bf-545e-aeef-35a531125f5f" :answer-field/id #uuid Equating the components of $i$, $j$, and $k$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{cos}⁡t=0 \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t=3 \\ 4\operatorname{sin}⁡t=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

From the first equality, $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(0,3,4)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(\frac{\pi }{2}).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+{(-\frac{3}{5})}^{2}+{(-\frac{4}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}+\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,3,4):$

$$

$$

$$

$$"] ["question-7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/id #uuid "7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b"] ["question-7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/math-academy-id "q-74850"] ["question-7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/problem "The equations of a curve $r(t)$ and its corresponding unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at an arbitrary point are given below. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at the point $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)).$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)⟩,\,t\ge 0 \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨t,\,1⟩,\,t\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1))$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)⟩ \\ ⟨\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)⟩ & =⟨\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}=\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}+t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other equation. Therefore, $P(\sqrt{2}\,,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2}+1))$ is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨t,\,1⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}})⟨t,\,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =-\frac{t}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨t,\,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟨1,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}[-⟨{t}^{2},\,t⟩+({t}^{2}+1)\cdot ⟨1,\,0⟩] \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,\,-t⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{({1}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}‖⟨1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,1⟩\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-1) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-7057aab9-4ddf-5b3b-9e59-0a11a291512b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-9023e46d-1d99-5286-baf3-0582b7f8b0a3" :answer-field/id #uuid ["question-7043d5b3-b126-54ab-a0bc-9816029b7532" :question/problem "Given the curve $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{3},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.
